A real myDAR iPhone walk, in local coordinates

Source: R/mydar_data.R
mydar_iphone_walk.Rd

Ryan Morton's outdoor walk of 2026-11-15: about 50 seconds and 25 m of track, recorded with the myDAR iPhone app and processed from the phone's capture files with the myDAR CLI at autodar commit a1388d8. It holds LiDAR points with their classes (vegetation split by height) and per-point sigma, the DEM, the track, 49 GPS fixes with residuals, and the accuracy figures. Camera points beyond LiDAR range are withheld by that processing, so every point is LiDAR. Read with read_mydar_walk(max_points = 6000), so it keeps 6,000 of the walk's 887,038 points. Use it to try the mydar_*_view() functions without the packages the readers need.

Usage

mydar_iphone_walk

Format

A mydar_walk; see read_mydar_walk for its elements.

Source

myDAR iPhone walk processed with the myDAR CLI (autodar a1388d8). data-raw/mydar_iphone_walk.R in the myIO repository builds it from a processed walk folder.

Details

The walk is shown in local coordinates only, moved there by subtraction (no rotation or scaling): x and y are meters from the walk's south-west corner and z is height above the lowest DEM (ground) cell. The subtracted origin, the project CRS and the feature layers are not included (origin is NA, crs is NA, features is empty). sigma_m, classes, the accuracy figures, GPS residuals and the trajectory (meters east, north and up of the first GPS fix) are as measured.
